q: Beyond letting air rise up through the house, what additional benefit do the Bahay Kubo's spaced bamboo floor slats provide?
o: They let dust simply be swept straight through to the ground below
They store heat like a thermal mass
They keep any air from entering the living space
They serve only as structural support for the roof
n: Bamboo Slats (Floor) are spaced flooring that allows air to rise through the house and provides an easy way to clean by sweeping dust directly below.

q: Occurring within or between solid bodies, which heat-transfer process moves thermal energy from one vibrating molecule to its immediate neighbor without any physical shift of the molecules themselves?
o: Convection
Emissivity
Radiation
Conduction
n: Conduction is the process in which heat energy is transferred from one vibrating molecule to the one immediately adjacent to it without any relative displacement of the molecules. This process takes place within or between solid bodies.

s: Thermal Forces — Air Entry and Escape
q: Because of thermal forces acting on a building, air typically enters through which openings and escapes through which?
o: It enters and leaves through one and the same opening
It enters through openings near the top and leaves through lower ones
It enters through lower-level openings and leaves through higher ones
It only ever enters through the roof
n: Due to thermal forces, air enters a building through the lower-level openings and escapes through openings located at higher portions of the building.

q: Which fixed architectural feature — a horizontal or vertical louver, for instance — is built specifically to block direct sunlight?
o: Solar screen
Venetian blind
Window shutter
Brise-soleil
n: A Brise-Soleil is a permanent architectural feature, such as a horizontal or vertical louver, designed to block direct sunlight.

q: In the seismic and thermal design of the Bahay na Bato, what does 'Structural Independence' actually refer to?
o: The stone ground floor carries the entire load of the house

A post-and-lintel timber frame carries the upper floor and roof, while the stone ground floor (arquitectura mestiza) is often non-load-bearing for those upper levels, letting the wood frame flex during earthquakes without collapsing
Timber frame and stone floor are fused into one rigid structural unit
There is no ground floor in the design at all
n: Structural Independence: the Bahay na Bato utilizes a post-and-lintel timber frame that supports the upper floor and roof. The stone ground floor (arquitectura mestiza) is often non-load bearing for the upper levels, allowing the wooden structure to sway during earthquakes without collapsing.

q: Of the two properties that govern radiant heat transfer at a surface, which one is a material's ability to give off thermal radiation?
o: Absorptivity
Reflectivity
Emissivity
Transmissivity
n: Emissivity is the ability of a material to give off thermal radiation. All materials emit heat; however, this varies in degree. Most building materials are good emitters of thermal radiation, but highly polished surfaces have low emissivity. The other property is absorptivity, the ability to take in radiant energy; reflectivity and transmissivity describe radiation that bounces off or passes through.

q: How is the 'Partition Effect' on airflow described?
o: Partitions never measurably affect airflow patterns
A partition set perpendicular to the wind always boosts airflow
A partition running parallel to the main airflow barely affects the pattern, while one set perpendicular to the wind produces a wind shadow
Any partition, regardless of orientation, blocks airflow entirely
n: Partition Effect: when a partition is placed parallel to the main flow of air, this has minimal influence on the pattern of air flow; but when located perpendicular to the incident wind, this creates a wind shadow.

q: Which side of a building is described as the one wind strikes first, experiencing higher pressure and generally staying cooler and better ventilated?
o: Leeward side
Windward side
Outlet side
Sheltered side
n: The windward side is the side facing into the wind. This is where the wind first hits a building or structure. It experiences higher air pressure and is typically cooler and more ventilated.

q: What made capiz shells a practical choice for window material in the Bahay na Bato?
o: Their sole purpose was decorative, with no functional benefit
They were tough enough to withstand typhoon winds and rain
They were the only material able to let sunlight through
They functioned thermally the same way a Trombe wall does
n: Capiz shells are durable enough to withstand the typhoon rains and winds.

q: Roughly 1361 W/m², which term names the average solar radiation received just outside Earth's atmosphere?
o: Solar collector
Solar insolation
Solar constant
Solar altitude
n: The Solar Constant is the average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere, approximately 1361 W/m².

q: Per PAGASA, which season — running June through October and bringing frequent heavy rain, storms, and typhoons — is this?
o: Tag-init
Amihan
Hot Dry Season
Habagat
n: Habagat (Southwest Monsoon) occurs from June to October and is characterized by frequent heavy rainfall, storms, and typhoons.

q: For walls as a component of an energy-efficient building, why is an East-West orientation generally discouraged in the tropics?
o: It cuts down on usable window area
That orientation causes the building to absorb more heat
It removes any possibility of cross ventilation
It simply raises construction costs
n: For walls, construction orientation should be analyzed based on the sun path. In tropical countries, the building should avoid facing the East-West direction because the building absorbs more heat.

s: Passive Cooling — Shading and Media Aguas
q: Under the principle of Shading and Media Aguas, what do deep roof overhangs and window awnings accomplish?
o: They let windows be left out of the design altogether
They seal the roof ridge so no air can move through it
They let the building envelope absorb the maximum possible solar heat
They let the building shade itself, keeping the envelope from absorbing solar heat
n: Shading and Media Aguas: Deep roof overhangs and window awnings ensure that the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat.

q: Which passive strategy relies on a building's orientation, materials, and thermal mass to gather and distribute heat without mechanical assistance?
o: A device that absorbs solar radiation and passes heat to a fluid
Passive Solar Heating
A system using pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
n: Passive Solar Heating utilizes building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to collect and distribute heat naturally.

q: What kind of air does Habagat carry, according to the source's discussion of wind patterns?
o: No measurable wind at all
Cool, dry air out of the northeast
Cold air limited to the winter solstice
Warm, moist air from the southwest, which brings heavier rain and humidity
n: Habagat brings warm, moist air from the southwest, resulting in heavier rains and humidity.

q: Besides light-colored roofing, what additional treatment is recommended for the roof as an element of an energy-efficient building?
o: Stripping away all roof overhangs
Adding heavier, denser roofing materials
Insulation backed with reflective foil
Painting the roof a dark shade to maximize absorption
n: For the roof, considerations include the materials used (cement, tiles, metal sheets, etc.), the way it is built/designed, the mass of the roof, putting insulation with reflective foil after the roof, and using light-colored roofs.

q: Which of the following names the vertical angle between the sun and the horizon at a given moment — essentially the sun's height above the horizon?
o: Azimuth
Meridian
Altitude
Longitude
n: Altitude is the height above the horizon — the vertical angle between the sun and the horizon at a given moment; higher angles occur in summer.

q: Spanning roughly 0° to 30° latitude, which atmospheric circulation cell has warm air rising at the equator, drifting toward 30°, then cooling and sinking to form subtropical high-pressure zones such as deserts?
o: Polar Cell
Trade Wind Cell
Ferrel Cell
Hadley Cell
n: The Hadley Cell (0°–30° latitude) has warm air rising at the equator and moving toward 30° latitude, where it cools and sinks, creating subtropical high-pressure zones (deserts).

q: Per the source's Passive Systems table, which mix of strategies applies to a hot-humid climate?
o: Maximum wind exposure, maximum internal airflow, minimum radiant heat gain
Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure
Minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, moderate internal airflow
Maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, maximum wind resistance
n: For a hot-humid climate, passive systems call for maximum wind exposure, maximum internal airflow, and minimum radiant heat gain.

q: Which cooling strategy pulls cool air in through low openings while letting warm air escape through high ones, taking advantage of the fact that warm air is less dense and rises?
o: A method that functions only during daytime hours
A principle used solely for cooling roofing materials
Stack Ventilation / Chimney Effect
A principle based entirely on pressure differences between two sides of a building
n: Warm air rises due to its lower density. Stack ventilation uses this principle to draw cool air from low openings while letting warm air escape through high-level openings like clerestory windows or roof vents. Stack ventilation works even without wind, driven purely by indoor-outdoor temperature differences, and is particularly useful at night or in urban areas where outdoor air movement is restricted. It is best combined with thermal mass and good insulation for enhanced performance.

q: Why, according to the source, does the sun's angle get progressively lower the further a site sits from the equator?
o: Because meridians converge as they near the equator
Because longitude decreases toward the poles
Because azimuth only applies within the tropics
Because the sun's rays hit the earth's curved surface at an increasingly oblique angle
n: The farther away from the equator, the lower the angle of the sun, because the sun's rays strike the convex surface of the earth more obliquely.

q: Under the Principle of Air Flow concerning inertia, what results from air's tendency to keep moving once set in motion?
o: It flows in a perfectly straight path no matter what obstacles it meets
It continues in its original direction until an intervening force is met
It loses all momentum the instant it enters a building
It halts immediately upon striking any obstacle
n: Air possesses inertia. Once set in motion, it tends to continue to flow in its initial direction until some intervening force is met.

q: Which landscaping feature — a mound or bank of earth used for insulation, privacy, or to redirect water — functions as a passive solar design element?
o: A cylindrical thermal mass wall built to store solar heat
Berm
An outdoor platform meant to capture ample sunlight
A glass-heavy room built to trap sunlight for warmth
n: A Berm is a mound or bank of earth used in landscaping for insulation, privacy, or to direct water flow.

q: According to the source, Philippine vernacular architecture is shaped by its capacity to adapt to what type of setting?
o: A temperate setting with four distinct seasons
A dry, cold, seismically quiet environment
A humid, hot, seismically active maritime environment
A desert setting with little rainfall
n: Philippine vernacular architecture is defined by its ability to adapt to a high-humidity, high-temperature, and seismically active maritime environment. Rather than resisting the elements with heavy mass, traditional structures utilize lightweight materials and permeability to achieve thermal comfort and structural resilience.

q: Falling around December 21 in the Northern Hemisphere, which day marks the sun's lowest noon position and thus the year's shortest daylight?
o: A day when daylight and darkness are roughly equal
The Winter Solstice
The day the sun reaches its highest noon position
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
n: The Winter Solstice is the day when the sun reaches its lowest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the shortest day of the year, typically around December 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: Occurring at night when land cools faster than adjacent water, producing surface airflow from land to sea and an upper return flow from sea to land, this pattern is what?
o: A wind pattern found only in mountainous terrain
Wind that develops during daylight, moving from sea toward land
Land Breeze
A result of the Ferrel Cell
n: A Land Breeze occurs at night: the land cools faster than the water, and the resulting movement of air is from land to sea at the surface, and from sea to land upward.

q: Which structure names an outdoor platform built to catch ample sunlight, often used for relaxing or getting solar exposure?
o: A glass-heavy room designed to trap sunlight
A thick, dark, glass-faced wall
Sun Deck
A mound or bank of earth for insulation or privacy
n: A Sun Deck is an outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight, often used for relaxation or solar access.

q: Made from nipa or anahaw, what role does the Bahay Kubo's thatch roofing serve?
o: It does away with the need for window openings
It is meant to absorb and hold as much solar heat as possible
The air pockets inside act as a natural insulator, keeping solar heat from radiating indoors
It exists purely as ornamentation with no practical function
n: Thatch Roofing is steeply pitched and made of nipa or anahaw. The air pockets within the thatch act as a natural thermal insulator, preventing solar heat from radiating into the interior.

q: Which heat-transfer process — capable of being either natural or forced — moves heat between a surface and a moving fluid by shifting molecules from one point in the fluid to another?
o: Absorptivity
Radiation
Conduction
Convection
n: Convection is the transfer of heat between a surface and a moving fluid, or the transfer of heat by movement of the molecules from one point in a fluid to another. Convection can either be natural or forced.

q: According to the source, what window height is the threshold for meaningfully effective indoor air movement?
o: 3.00 meters
2.00 meters
0.50 meters
1.10 meters
n: Window heights are significant for effective indoor air movement when those measure up to 1.10 meters. No additional benefit for direct occupancy comfort is derived if openings are higher, though higher openings can reduce heat loads on the ceiling.

q: Which window covering can be tilted open or closed to adjust light and privacy?
o: A mesh or fabric layer over a window to cut solar gain
Shutter Blind
A device or structure that filters sunlight to reduce glare and heat
A fixed feature built to block direct sun
n: A Shutter Blind is an adjustable window covering that can be tilted to control light and privacy.

q: In the Bahay na Bato, what function does 'The Volada' serve?
o: Sliding panels set beneath the main window sills
A latticework frame holding translucent capiz shells
Pierced wooden panels above doors or walls that let light and air circulate
An overhanging gallery that shields the ground floor from rain and sun while letting air circulate around the main living rooms
n: The Volada is an overhanging gallery that protects the ground floor from rain and direct sun, while also acting as a circulation path that allows air to wrap around the main living rooms.

q: Which property — under which most construction materials, whatever their color, behave like a 'black body' — is the capacity of a material to absorb radiant energy and convert it into other forms?
o: The height of the sun above the horizon
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A material's ability to give off thermal radiation
Absorptivity
n: Absorptivity is the capacity of a material to absorb radiant energy and convert it to other forms of energy. Most construction materials, regardless of color, act as a 'black body.' Most thermal radiation the material intercepts is absorbed.

q: The source gives what average temperature range for the Philippines' tropical maritime climate?
n: The Philippines has an average temperature of 25°C to 32°C (77°F to 89°F) — hot and humid throughout the year, with very little variation. The warmest months are typically March to May (dry season peak).

q: Which side of a building is sheltered from the wind — opposite its direction — typically experiencing lower pressure, calmer air, and outward airflow during cross ventilation?
o: The side facing true north no matter the wind direction
The side that always carries the highest air pressure
The leeward side
The side the wind strikes first
n: The leeward side is the side sheltered from the wind, or opposite the wind's direction. It experiences lower air pressure and often calmer air. Air tends to exit from this side during cross ventilation.

q: What are 'Calado' in the context of the Bahay na Bato?
o: A latticework panel sealing windows completely with capiz shells
A sliding panel set beneath a window sill
Pierced wooden panels above each room's doors or walls that let light and air move through the house
An overhanging gallery that circulates air around the main living rooms
n: Calado are pierced wooden panels above doors or walls of each room that allow light and air to circulate in the house.

q: Which term names a house purpose-built to use solar energy for heating, lighting, or power?
o: A system that heats air or water using solar energy
A device that absorbs solar radiation and passes heat to a fluid
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
Solar House
n: A Solar House is a house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power.

q: Per PAGASA's seasonal breakdown, when does the Hot Dry Season (Tag-init) fall?
o: November through February, cool and dry
March through May
December through February only
June through October, wet and stormy
n: Hot Dry Season (Tag-init) occurs from March to May.

q: Regarding wall materials for energy-efficient buildings, why are heavy, dense materials typically discouraged?
o: They cannot structurally support a roof
They cost more than lightweight alternatives across the board
They block ventilation entirely
They absorb heat slowly and release it just as slowly, leading to heat gain and retention
n: Heavy/dense wall materials should be avoided because they absorb heat and release it at a very slow pace, which results in heat gain and heat retention.

q: Which geographic coordinate marks east-west position and, combined with latitude, is used to pin down solar position?
o: Meridian
Latitude
Azimuth
Longitude
n: Longitude is a geographic coordinate specifying east-west position; used with latitude to determine solar position.

q: Which piece of equipment gathers solar radiation and passes the heat along to a fluid?
o: A system that harnesses solar energy to heat air or water
Solar Collector
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A house built to capture solar energy for heat, light, or power
n: A Solar Collector is a device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid.

q: Owing to elevation, which Philippine locations does the source cite as having noticeably cooler regional microclimates?
o: Central Luzon
Bicol and Eastern Visayas
Baguio or Tagaytay
Metro Manila
n: Cooler climates occur in elevated areas like Baguio or Tagaytay, while hotter, drier zones occur in areas like Central Luzon, and more rainfall occurs on eastern-facing coasts (e.g., Bicol, Eastern Visayas) due to exposure to trade winds.

q: For flooring in an energy-efficient building, what quality should the chosen material have?
o: High emissivity paired with high infiltration of hot air
Uniformly high density, whatever the material
Low emissivity with minimal infiltration of hot air
It must always be timber and never concrete
n: For the floor, the type of material used is usually concrete or timber, and materials of low emissivity and no infiltration of hot air should be used.

q: Measured clockwise from true south, which term describes the sun's position as projected onto a horizontal plane?
o: Longitude
Latitude
Altitude
Azimuth
n: Azimuth is the position of the sun with respect to its projection on a horizontal plane. This is measured from true south and running clockwise.

q: Spanning roughly 30° to 60° latitude, with air moving poleward near the surface and equatorward aloft, and driven less by thermal forces than by neighboring cells, which circulation cell is this?
o: Hadley Cell
Polar Cell
Trade Wind Cell
Ferrel Cell
n: The Ferrel Cell (30°–60° latitude) has air flowing poleward near the surface and equatorward at high altitudes. It is less thermally driven and more influenced by adjacent cells.

q: Per the Passive Systems table, which combination best fits a hot-dry climate strategy?
o: Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure
Maximum wind exposure and maximum internal airflow
Maximum thermal retention and maximum radiant heat gain
Minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, moderate internal airflow
n: For a hot-dry climate, passive systems call for minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, and moderate internal airflow.

q: How does the source say Stack Ventilation can actually be built into a design?
o: By using only mechanical fans instead of passive openings
By sealing off every low-level opening and relying purely on high vents
By tearing out all vertical shafts and stairwells
By pairing low inlets (windows near the floor) with high outlets (roof vents, clerestories, solar chimneys), sometimes using light wells or atriums with high exhaust points
n: Stack ventilation can be achieved by including low-level inlets (like windows near the floor) and high-level outlets (like roof vents, clerestories, or solar chimneys). Light wells or atriums with high exhaust openings can be used; in taller buildings, this can be amplified with vertical shafts or stairwells.

q: Which latitude is assigned to the equator, and which to the North Pole?
o: 1 deg. and 90 deg. N
1 deg. and 180 deg. N
0 deg. and 180 deg. N
0 deg. and 90 deg. N
n: The equator is designated 1 deg. latitude while the north pole is at 90 deg. N latitude.

s: Principles of Air Flow — Least Resistance
q: Per the source's third principle of airflow, air moves along which kind of path?
o: A path driven only by temperature, never pressure
The path of greatest resistance
A completely random path
The path of least resistance
n: Air flows through the path of least resistance.

q: Which passive solar feature is a thick wall, painted dark and faced in glass, meant to absorb heat by day and release it at night?
o: An outdoor platform built to catch abundant sunlight
A mound or bank of earth for insulation or privacy
Drum Wall
A glass-heavy room designed to catch sunlight
n: A Drum Wall is a thermal mass wall, often cylindrical, designed to absorb and store solar heat during the day and release it at night.

q: In the Bahay Kubo, what do the 'Haligi' refer to?
o: Woven bamboo or rattan panels allowing air to filter through
Massive wood trunks or bamboo poles raising the living area, guarding against dampness, flooding, and pests while letting air ventilate underneath
Steeply pitched roofing made of nipa or anahaw
Spaced flooring letting air rise through the house
n: Haligi are massive wooden trunks or bamboo poles that elevate the living area. This protects against dampness, seasonal flooding, and pests while allowing for sub-floor ventilation.

q: Occurring twice yearly around March 21 and September 23, when day and night are roughly equal in length, this event is called what?
o: The longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
Equinox
The shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere
n: An Equinox occurs twice a year when day and night are approximately equal in length, around March 21 (vernal equinox) and September 23 (autumnal equinox).

q: How does the pressure on a building's windward side compare with its leeward side?
o: Both sides experience identical pressure at all times
Windward pressure runs negative while leeward runs positive
Windward pressure is high and positive, while leeward pressure is negative
Pressure differences only matter for stack ventilation, not for wind-driven flow
n: An important characteristic of wind force is that the windward side has a positive high pressure, while the leeward side has a negative pressure.

q: As a device for controlling sunlight, what best describes a Sunshade?
o: A mesh or fabric layer over windows cutting solar gain while keeping visibility
A device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight to cut heat gain and glare
A permanent louver, horizontal or vertical, fixed to block direct sun
A solid or louvered panel closed over a window
n: A Sunshade is a device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight to reduce heat gain and glare.

q: How was the Bahay na Bato's living platform kept away from the damp ground?
o: By elevating it using bamboo poles, as in the Bahay Kubo
By setting it on a concrete slab foundation
By building it directly on grade, with no elevation at all
By raising it on a stone ground floor
n: The Bahay na Bato's living platform was elevated from the damp ground by a stone on the ground floor.

q: What takes place during natural convection once a fluid contacts a heat source?
o: It sinks immediately and grows denser
It absorbs heat, expands, loses density, and rises, drawing cooler fluid in to replace it and setting up natural circulation
It stops moving altogether
It transfers only through molecule-to-molecule contact
n: Natural convection occurs when fluid comes in contact with a heat source: it absorbs heat, expands, becomes less dense, and rises, allowing a cooler portion of the fluid to meet the heat source, which in turn rises and causes a natural circulation. When air is blown against the surface of a hot fluid, it cools fast.

q: For louvers, slats, and overhangs functioning as wind deflectors, at what level should they sit to steer airflow into the occupied zones of a building?
o: Only along the roofline
At a higher level
Right at floor level, low down
They shouldn't be angled at all
n: Louvers, slats, and overhangs should be positioned at a higher level to redirect air motion onto the occupancy zones of buildings.

q: Which sun-control device is a mesh or fabric layer stretched over windows to reduce solar heat gain while preserving visibility?
o: A solid or louvered panel closed over a window
A permanent horizontal or vertical louver fixed to block direct sun
Solar Screen
An outdoor platform for catching ample sunlight
n: A Solar Screen is a mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visibility.

q: Protected by rejas (iron grilles), which sliding panels sit beneath the main window sills of the Bahay na Bato, allowing low-level air intake even with the main windows shut for privacy or during a storm?
o: Latticework panels framed with translucent capiz shells
Pierced wooden panels above doors letting light and air through
A thick, dark-painted glass wall absorbing solar heat
Ventanillas
n: Ventanillas are sliding panels located beneath the main window sills. They are protected by rejas (iron grilles) and allow for low-level air intake even when main windows are closed for privacy or during rain.

q: Described as capable of absorbing radiation at the highest possible emittance, this ideal material is known by what name?
o: A material with the lowest possible emittance
A material reserved solely for solar collectors
Black Body
A material that reflects all radiant energy striking it
n: The black body is an ideal material which can absorb radiation with the highest possible emittance.

q: Which relative humidity range does the source assign to the Philippines, noting it climbs especially high during the rainy season?
o: 90% to 100% year-round
n: Relative humidity in the Philippines ranges from 70% to 90%, and is especially high during the rainy season.

q: As applied to architecture, what does Bernoulli's Principle explain?
o: Warm air always sinks while cool air always rises
Air pressure holds steady no matter the speed
As air speeds up, its pressure falls — air moving faster above ground level, where obstacles are fewer, has lower pressure, and this difference can help draw fresh air through a building
Wind direction is unaffected by nearby buildings, vegetation, or terrain
n: Bernoulli's principle is a fundamental concept in fluid dynamics explaining how differences in wind speed can drive air movement. As air flows faster, its pressure drops. In architecture, air higher above the ground — where there are fewer obstacles — typically moves more quickly and has lower pressure; this pressure difference can help pull fresh air through a building. Nearby structures, vegetation, or terrain can block or channel this airflow.

q: Under the source's Passive Cooling Principles for modern buildings, along which axis should a building's long axis run, and for what reason?
o: Diagonally, at 45 degrees to the compass, purely for visual effect
North to South, to catch the most morning and afternoon sun
It makes no difference — orientation has no bearing on solar heat gain
East to West, minimizing wall area exposed to low-angle morning and afternoon sun while maximizing exposure to the prevailing Amihan and Habagat winds
n: Building Orientation: Strategic placement is critical. The long axis of the building should run from East to West. This minimizes the wall surface area exposed to the low-angle morning and afternoon sun while maximizing the facade's ability to catch the prevailing Amihan (Northeast) and Habagat (Southwest) winds.

q: Which system uses solar energy specifically to heat air or water for residential or commercial purposes?
o: Solar-Heating System
A house built to capture solar energy for heat, light, or power
A method relying on orientation, materials, and thermal mass to distribute heat naturally
A device absorbing solar radiation and passing heat to a fluid
n: A Solar-Heating System is a system using solar energy to heat air or water for residential or commercial use.

q: About how many typhoons enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) each year, and how many typically make landfall?
o: Roughly 5 enter the PAR annually, with 1–2 making landfall
Roughly 2 enter the PAR annually, with none making landfall
Roughly 20 enter the PAR annually, with 8–10 making landfall
Roughly 50 enter the PAR annually, with 30 making landfall
n: An average of 20 typhoons enters the Philippine Area of Responsibility annually; 8–10 of these make landfall. The most active typhoon months are July to October.

q: Regarding windows in an energy-efficient building, how is window area related to heat gain?
o: Heat gain depends solely on window color, not size
A larger window area always cuts down heat gain
Window area bears no relation to heat gain
A larger window area produces greater heat gain
n: For windows, area matters: the bigger the area, the larger the heat gain.

q: Important for pinpointing solar noon at a given location, which term names a line of longitude?
o: Altitude
Latitude
Meridian
Azimuth
n: A Meridian is a line of longitude; important for determining solar noon at a given location.

q: Because the equator receives more solar energy than the poles, what results?
o: Warm equatorial air sinks while cold polar air rises
Warm equatorial air rises, creating low pressure, while cold polar air sinks, creating high pressure — the resulting pressure gradients drive air movement
Air pressure stays uniform across the whole planet
The Coriolis effect cancels out any pressure gradient
n: The equator receives more solar energy than the poles. Warm air at the equator rises (low pressure), while cold air at the poles sinks (high pressure). This creates pressure gradients that drive air movement.

s: Problems in Areas with Tropical Climates
q: Which of these is identified as a problem found in tropical-climate regions?
o: Steady cool temperatures throughout the year
High temperature, high humidity, sluggish wind speeds, and heavy rainy-season precipitation
A near-total absence of insects and rodents
Low humidity paired with brisk wind speeds
n: Problems in areas with tropical climates include high temperature level (heat), high humidity levels, slow wind velocities, high precipitation levels during rainy days, high incidence of typhoons, and abundance of insects and rodents due to damp ground conditions.

q: Which ventilation strategy uses pressure differences between opposite sides of a building — air entering a windward opening and leaving through a leeward one — to move air through interior spaces?
o: A strategy relying purely on stack effect, without any wind pressure
A method aimed only at cooling a roof cavity
Cross Ventilation
A strategy that only functions in still, urban settings with no wind
n: Cross ventilation relies on wind pressure differences between opposite sides of a building to move air through a space. Air enters from a windward opening and exits through a leeward opening, creating a cooling breeze. It is highly effective in tropical climates with consistent wind patterns and when the building is oriented to catch prevailing winds.

q: Which diagram plots the sun's path across the sky through the year, helping guide building orientation and shading decisions?
o: A line of longitude used for determining solar noon
Solar Path Diagram (Solar Chart)
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A geographic coordinate for north-south position
n: A Solar Path Diagram (Solar chart) is a diagram plotting the sun's path across the sky over the year, aiding in building orientation and shading design.

q: Covering roughly 60° to 90° latitude, with cold air sinking at the poles and flowing equatorward, which circulation cell is this?
o: Coriolis Cell
Hadley Cell
Ferrel Cell
Polar Cell
n: The Polar Cell (60°–90° latitude) has cold air sinking at the poles and flowing equatorward.

q: Per the Passive Systems table, which mix of strategies characterizes a cool climate?
o: Minimum radiant heat gain paired with moderate internal airflow
Maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, and maximum wind resistance
Maximum wind exposure with minimum thermal retention
Moderate thermal retention with only slight wind exposure
n: For a cool climate, passive systems call for maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, and maximum wind resistance.

s: Night Ventilation of Thermal Mass (Night Purging)
q: Also known as night purging, which cooling technique draws cooler night air into a building to flush the day's stored heat out of thermal mass like walls and floors, so the building starts cooler the next day?
o: Sealing the building at night to trap the day's heat for later use
A mechanical air-conditioning process run only in daytime
A process that only works where day and night temperatures are the same
Night Ventilation of Thermal Mass
n: At night, cooler outdoor air is drawn into the building to flush out the day's accumulated heat from thermal mass (e.g., walls and floors). This prepares the building to stay cooler the next day. It is a sustainable, environmentally friendly cooling method relying on natural ventilation rather than energy-intensive air conditioning, and is very effective in climates with high daytime temperatures but cooler nights. It works best with good daytime shading and cross ventilation.

q: At roughly what latitude does the source place Metropolitan Manila?
o: 0 deg. (the Equator)
23.5 deg. N
66.5 deg. N
14.5 deg. N
n: Metropolitan Manila would generally be in the 14.5 deg. N latitude.

s: Wind Flows Due to Heat Exchange
q: What property of air explains why wind arises from heat exchange, per the source?
o: Air temperature shifts more slowly than the ground's
Air movement is driven solely by the Coriolis effect
Air is incapable of carrying temperature at all
Air can transport temperature, and its temperature shifts faster than the ground's
n: Air has the ability to transport temperature. One characteristic of air is that its temperature changes faster than the ground temperature.

q: Which passive design feature is a thick, dark-painted wall faced in glass that absorbs solar heat and radiates it into the building's interior?
o: A mound or bank of earth used in landscaping
An outdoor platform meant for relaxation or solar exposure
A room with extensive glazing designed to catch sunlight
Trombe Wall
n: A Trombe Wall is a passive solar building design feature consisting of a thick wall painted dark and faced with glass, which absorbs solar heat and radiates it into the building.

q: As part of the Bahay Kubo's permeable envelope, what are 'Sawali Walls'?
o: Massive wood trunks that raise the living area
Woven bamboo or rattan panels that let air filter through
Spaced bamboo flooring meant for ventilation and cleaning
Steeply pitched thatch roofing
n: Sawali Walls are woven bamboo or rattan panels that permit air filtration, as part of the Bahay Kubo's Permeable Building Envelope.

q: Heat, a form of energy arising from the random motion of molecules, is transmitted through which three processes?
o: Insulation, ventilation, and infiltration
Radiation, refraction, and reflection
Conduction, convection, and radiation
Absorption, emission, and diffusion
n: Heat is a form of energy generated by the random motion of molecules. There are three processes by which heat is transmitted: conduction, convection, and radiation.

q: Air entering a building through a positive-pressure zone opening exits through an opening in which zone?
o: Another positive-pressure zone
Only through roof vents
The negative-pressure zone
There's no relationship between pressure zone and where air enters or exits
n: Air enters the building through openings located in the positive pressure zone and exits through openings located at the negative pressure zone.

q: Which item is a solid or louvered panel that closes over a window to manage light and heat?
o: An adjustable window covering that tilts to control light and privacy
Shutter Panel
A mesh or fabric layer over windows to cut solar gain
A device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight generally
n: A Shutter Panel is a solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows to control light and heat.

q: Together with latticed vents fitted beneath them, what do the Bahay na Bato's wide eaves (alero) provide?
o: Structural support solely for the stone ground floor
A mounting location for solar collectors
A space specifically engineered to have zero ventilation
Sun shading for window openings, while the latticed vents beneath let breeze into the roof cavity
n: The wide eaves (alero) provide the necessary sun shading for window openings, and the underside of the wide eaves has fitted latticed vents that allow breeze to enter the roof cavity.

q: Measured as a temperature at a material's surface and responsible for how the earth receives heat from the sun, which heat-transfer process moves heat through space via electromagnetic waves?
o: Solar Constant
Convection
Conduction
Radiation
n: Radiation is the transfer of heat through a space by electro-magnetic waves and is measured as temperature at the surface of the material. The earth receives its heat from the sun by radiation.

q: What happens when vertical wall projections (vertical deflectors) sit parallel to the wind's incident direction?
o: They have no measurable effect on airflow
They only function when placed perpendicular to the main airflow
They create a wind shadow
They prevent wind shadows and dead air zones from forming
n: Vertical deflectors — vertical wall projections placed parallel to the incident wind — prevent wind shadows or dead zones of air. But when placed perpendicular to the main flow, the same system can create a wind shadow. Placing openings at the foot of partitions will induce air flow.

q: Facing a sunlit window directly, a person may experience visual discomfort caused by what, and how is it removed?
o: Excess absorptivity, removed by painting the wall a dark color
Glare, removed once sun-control devices are put in place
Excess humidity, removed by adding a solar screen
Excess ventilation, removed by shutting all the windows
n: To a person directly facing a sunlit window, visual discomfort may be due to glare. When sun control devices are provided, glare would be eliminated.

q: Used to completely shut windows at night or during a storm, which latticework panels frame the Bahay na Bato's translucent capiz shells?
o: A sliding panel set beneath a window sill
An overhanging gallery shielding the ground floor
Concha
A pierced wooden panel set above a doorway
n: Concha are latticework panels that framed the translucent capiz shells; they were used to completely shut windows at night or during a storm.

q: Essential for natural lighting, heating, and renewable systems in buildings, what is Solar Energy defined as?
o: A device absorbing solar radiation and passing heat to a fluid
A house built to capture solar energy for heat, light, or power
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
Radiant energy given off by the sun
n: Solar Energy is radiant energy from the sun, essential for natural lighting, heating, and renewable energy systems in buildings.

q: Bringing cool, dry air from November through February, which of PAGASA's seasons is this?
o: Tag-init
Southwest Monsoon
Habagat
Amihan
n: Amihan (Northeast Monsoon) occurs from November to February and brings cool, dry air.

q: Describing air that speeds up while passing through a narrow or constricted space — thereby dropping pressure there — which fluid-dynamics principle is often used to boost natural ventilation through tapered corridors or narrow openings?
o: The tendency for warm air to rise owing to lower density
A principle stating air slows and gains pressure in a constricted space
The deflection of moving air caused by Earth's rotation
Venturi Effect
n: The Venturi Effect is a principle in fluid dynamics where air (or fluid) speeds up when it flows through a narrow or constricted space, causing a drop in pressure in that area. In architecture, it can be intentionally used to enhance natural ventilation by guiding wind through narrow openings or tapered corridors, increasing airflow speed and helping draw air through indoor spaces.

q: Using high-pitched roofs and open transoms (espejitos), how is the Stack Effect (natural buoyancy) put into practice as a modern passive cooling approach?
o: Hot air trapped at the roof ridge with no way out cools the interior purely by radiation
Hot air rises and escapes through the roof ridge, drawing cooler air in through lower openings such as the ventanillas
Cool air is mechanically pumped from the roof ridge down to the ground floor
Roof pitch has no bearing on air movement — only wall material matters
n: Stack Effect (Natural Buoyancy): By using high-pitched roofs and open transoms (espejitos), hot air is allowed to rise and escape through the roof ridge, pulling cooler air in through lower openings like the ventanillas.

q: Illustrated by a solar collector, water tank, pump, and boiler setup, what sets an Active Solar-Heating System apart?
o: It functions only at night
It uses building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to gather and spread heat passively
It relies entirely on radiation, with no fluid transfer involved
It employs mechanical equipment such as pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids
n: An Active Solar-Heating System uses mechanical equipment like pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids.

q: What does Amihan bring, and why does this make it favorable for natural ventilation design?
o: Warm, moist air from the southwest, bringing heavier rain and humidity
Cool, dry air from the northeast
Hot, humid air straight from the equator
No wind whatsoever, just stillness
n: Amihan brings cool, dry air from the northeast, which is good for natural ventilation design.

q: In the source's ranking of window shading coefficients from least to most desirable, which type ranks as most desirable?
o: Reflective glass
Clear glass with blinds
Double glass
Window with awning
n: The source ranks shading coefficient of window types from least to most desirable as: 1. Double glass, 2. Clear glass with blinds, 3. Reflective glass, 4. Window with awning (most desirable).

q: Which approach precisely calculates solar angles — azimuth and altitude — using spherical trigonometry, useful for detailed architectural analysis and design?
o: Solar Constant
Meridian
Solar Path Diagram
Sun Path
n: Sun Path refers to solar angles made up of azimuth and altitude, which can be precisely calculated by methods of spherical trigonometry — useful when detailed solar position and angles are required for architectural analysis and design.

q: Given that the Coriolis Effect deflects moving air to the right in the Northern Hemisphere due to Earth's rotation, which direction does it deflect air in the Southern Hemisphere?
o: Straight upward
There's no deflection south of the equator
Also to the right
To the left
n: Due to Earth's rotation, moving air is deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. This deflection shapes wind patterns and circulation cells.

q: Which of the following appears among the Design Objectives in Tropical Climates?
o: Cutting off all natural daylight from interior spaces
Maximizing heat gain, maximizing ventilation while guarding against typhoon winds, avoiding unnecessary humidity increases, ensuring good drainage, and protecting spaces from insects and rodents
Minimizing ventilation while maximizing humidity
Maximizing heat gain while minimizing drainage
n: Design Objectives in Tropical Climates include: maximize heat gain (loss); maximize ventilation but protect from typhoon wind; prevent unnecessary increase in humidity levels; have a good drainage system to accommodate high annual precipitation; and protect spaces from insects and rodents.

q: According to the source, how can Cross Ventilation be built into a design?
o: By sealing every window and depending entirely on mechanical ventilation
By placing every opening on a single wall only
By positioning windows, vents, or doors on opposite or adjacent walls so air moves across rooms, aided by louvered or operable windows and open floor plans or interior transoms
By removing interior transoms and open floor plans altogether
n: Cross ventilation can be achieved by positioning windows, vents, or doors on opposite or adjacent walls to allow airflow across rooms. Louvered or operable windows help regulate air entry and exit. Open floor plans or interior transoms allow airflow between rooms.

q: Which geographic coordinate marks north-south position and shapes solar angles and the length of daylight?
o: Azimuth
Meridian
Longitude
Latitude
n: Latitude is a geographic coordinate specifying north-south position, which influences solar angles and daylight length.

s: Principles of Air Flow — Pressure Gradient
q: Which of the following is listed among the source's Principles of Air Flow?
o: Air always moves against the wind's original direction
Air moves from a low-pressure area toward a high-pressure one
Air pressure has no real bearing on air movement
Air moves from a high-pressure area toward a low-pressure one
n: One principle of air flow is that air flows from a high-pressure to a low-pressure area.

q: Per the Passive Systems table, which combination fits a temperate climate strategy?
o: Maximum thermal retention paired with maximum wind resistance
Maximum wind exposure with minimum radiant heat gain
Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure for humidity control, and moderate internal airflow
Minimum radiant heat gain only, with airflow left unconsidered
n: For a temperate climate, passive systems call for moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure (humidity control), and moderate internal airflow.

q: What is the 'diurnal swing,' and why does thermal mass need it to be high in order to work as an effective passive strategy?
o: The angle between azimuth and altitude at solar noon
The gap between summer and winter solar altitude, unrelated to thermal mass
The total solar radiation a black body absorbs over 24 hours
The gap between daytime and nighttime outdoor temperatures, which must be large for thermal mass to work well for passive heating and cooling
n: Diurnal swing is the difference between daytime and nighttime outdoor temperatures. This must be high for thermal mass to be an effective passive cooling and heating strategy; thermal mass can be used with nocturnal convective cooling or 'night cooling' to passively cool buildings.

q: Typically falling around June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere, which day marks the sun's highest noon position and the year's longest daylight?
o: A day when daylight and darkness are roughly equal
The day the sun sits at its lowest noon point, giving the shortest day
Summer Solstice
A line of longitude important for solar noon
n: The Summer Solstice is the day when the sun reaches its highest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the longest day of the year, typically around June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: Which wind pattern develops as daytime heating begins, with land warming faster than water and air moving upward and seaward, so wind blows from sea toward land?
o: A wind pattern limited to polar regions
Wind that forms at night as land cools faster than water, moving land to sea
The deflection of air caused by the Coriolis effect
Sea Breeze
n: A Sea Breeze occurs as daytime heating begins: the land warms more rapidly than the water. Upward expansion of the air column over the land causes a seaward movement of air upward, and wind from the sea directed toward land develops.

q: Which room, built with extensive glazing to capture sunlight for warmth and light, is this?
o: A mound or bank of earth used for insulation
An outdoor platform meant to catch ample sunlight
Solarium / Sunroom
A thermal mass wall built to store solar heat
n: A Solarium / Sunroom is a room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight for warmth and light.
